newsitem.title: USA: U.S. business inventories rise 0.7 percent in June.
newsitem.headline: U.S. business inventories rise 0.7 percent in June.

text.p: Inventories held by businesses took their biggest jump in more than two years in June mostly because of a bulge in unsold goods held by wholesalers, the Commerce Department said on Thursday.

Total business inventories rose 0.7 percent in June to a seasonally adjusted $1.026 trillion after a 0.2 percent rise in May, the department said. Total sales rebounded sharply by 0.7 percent to $747.86 billion after a 0.5 percent drop.

The 0.7 percent rise in June inventories, which was slightly larger than the 0.6 percent gain Wall Street economists had expected, was the largest since a 0.8 percent gain in April 1995, the department said.
But the inventory-to-sales ratio, which measures how long it would take to deplete stocks at the current sales pace, held at a fairly low 1.37 months' worth in June.

The June inventory increase was led by a five-year high 1.9 percent jump in wholesalers' unsold goods, to $263.93 billion, the department said. Retail inventories rose 0.2 percent in June to $317.22 billion and manufacturers' inventories were up 0.3 percent to $444.8 billion.
At auto dealerships, inventories rose a scant 0.1 percent in June to $87.7 billion.
